title: The Great Outdoors
about: A family's quiet lake holiday is wrecked when the rich, loud brother-in-law and his family turn up.
cue: Serve the main when Chet takes on the Old 96er.
faces: Quiet week at the lake, I said. Then Roman showed up with lobsters.

    StartersLakeside crumbed fish bites with tartarePanko crumbed flathead bites with homemade tartare sauceHow to make it500g flathead fillets50g plain flour2 eggs, beaten120g panko breadcrumbs500ml vegetable oil, for frying150g mayonnaise1 tbsp capers, chopped2 tbsp chopped dill pickles1 tbsp chopped parsley2 lemonsCut the flathead into bite-size pieces.Toss in flour, dip in egg, then coat in panko.Shallow fry in the oil at 180°C, turning once, until golden. Drain.Mix the mayonnaise with the capers, pickles, parsley and a squeeze of lemon.Serve hot with the tartare and lemon wedges.Chet's Wisconsin fried cheese curdsWisconsin cheese curds, guarded from the raccoons in the binsHow to make it500g cheese curds or mild cheddar, cubed150g plain flour1 tsp sweet paprika1 tsp salt1 egg250ml cold soda water2 L vegetable oil, for frying150ml ranch dressingWhisk the flour, paprika and salt with the egg and soda water into a smooth batter.Heat the oil to 180°C.Dip the cheese in the batter and fry in batches for 1 to 2 minutes until golden.Drain and serve hot with the ranch.MainsThe Old 96er rump steakBig rump steak with garlic butter, onion rings, roast potatoes, ranch wedgeHow to make it1.5kg rump steak4 tbsp vegetable oil1kg potatoes, halved60g butter2 garlic cloves, crushed400g frozen onion rings1 iceberg lettuce, cut into wedges150ml ranch dressingRub the steak with oil and salt. Toss the potatoes in oil.Roast the potatoes at 220°C.Grill the steak over high heat for medium rare.Rest the steak. Bake the onion rings.Melt the butter with the garlic. Drizzle the lettuce wedges with ranch.Slice the steak thickly, pour over the garlic butter and serve.Roman's big shot barbecue chicken with potato saladRoman insists on paying, then tells you what it costHow to make it4 chicken marylands150ml barbecue sauce1 tsp smoked paprika800g chat potatoes4 tbsp whole egg mayonnaise3 tbsp sour cream2 spring onions, sliced1 bunch dillsalt and pepper, to tasteBoil the potatoes until tender, drain and cool a little.Toss the potatoes with the mayonnaise, sour cream, spring onion, chopped dill and salt.Rub the chicken with paprika and salt and grill over medium coals, turning, until nearly cooked.Brush with barbecue sauce and grill until sticky. Serve with the potato salad.SweetsBald-headed bear blueberry pieBlueberry pie with a lemon scented filling and pastry crustHow to make it750g frozen blueberries135g caster sugar3 tbsp cornflour1 lemon2 sheets of shortcrust pastry1 egg, beaten1 L vanilla ice cream, to serveToss the blueberries with most of the sugar, cornflour and the lemon zest and juice.Line a 23cm pie dish with one pastry sheet and fill with the berries. Cover with the second sheet, crimp the edges and cut slits on top.Brush with egg and sprinkle with the remaining sugar.Bake at 200°C, then at 180°C until bubbling.Cool, then serve with ice cream.Lake cabin campfire s'moresToasted marshmallow, chocolate and caramel sandwiched between biscuitsHow to make it24 plain sweet wheatmeal biscuits100g milk chocolate100g dark chocolate4 tbsp caramel sauce16 large marshmallowsLay half the biscuits on a lined tray. Top some with milk chocolate and the rest with dark chocolate and a little caramel.Thread the marshmallows onto skewers and toast over a fire or gas flame until golden, or grill on a tray.Put marshmallows on each chocolate biscuit and press another biscuit on top.
